forces.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Energy Prices Weigh on Spending
forces.description: Ongoing geopolitical tensions and the resulting rise in energy and fuel prices continue to negatively impact consumer confidence and their appetite for spending in the Netherlands, contributing to cautious retail sales growth despite improved purchasing power.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: E-commerce Sustains Retail Growth and Market Share Expansion
forces.description: E-commerce continues to be the primary growth engine for the Dutch retail sector, with expected turnover growth of 4.5% in 2026. This ongoing long-term shift towards online shopping is steadily increasing e-commerce's share of total retail sales, strengthening its position against traditional channels.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Profit Margins Squeezed by Rising Costs and Fierce Competition
forces.description: Dutch retailers face significant pressure on profit margins due to rising sourcing, logistics, and labor costs across food, non-food, and e-commerce segments. Fierce competition and price-sensitive consumers limit the ability to pass on these higher costs, making profitable growth increasingly difficult for many operators.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Multichannel Retailers Outpace Online-Only Competitors
forces.description: For the first time since 2022, online sales growth among multichannel retailers has surpassed that of online-only retailers in the Netherlands. This trend is driven by shifting consumer demand towards segments where multichannel retailers, particularly supermarkets and drugstores, have strong positions and by their strengthened digital capabilities, combining e-commerce convenience with physical store advantages.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Food Prices Expected to Rise Due to Drought and Geopolitical Tensions
forces.description: Despite a recent easing in food inflation, drought-related supply disruptions and ongoing geopolitical tensions are expected to push food prices higher again later in 2026. This presents a key risk for retailers' input costs and consumer spending power, particularly impacting the grocery sector.
forces.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

forces.title: Higher Interest Rates Dampen Consumer Durable Sales
forces.description: Prospects for higher interest rates are a significant headwind for Norway's retail sector, particularly affecting turnover growth in consumer durables. This financial pressure influences household spending decisions on big-ticket items, offsetting some of the positive momentum from tourism and solid household finances.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Flat Headcounts and Unchanged Retail Margins Expected
forces.description: Retail trade contacts in Norway plan to keep headcounts flat through autumn, citing spare capacity within the sector. Furthermore, retail margins are reported as little changed, indicating a challenging environment where efficiency measures are easing staffing needs and profitability remains stagnant.
forces.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

forces.title: Extreme Weather Impacts Raw Material Availability and Costs
forces.description: Extreme heat and very low rainfall in Western Europe are affecting harvests and the availability and cost of raw materials. This volatility has significant implications for food and drink production costs upstream, which will transmit to grocery retailers through higher sourcing costs and potential supply disruptions.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Evolving EU Packaging Regulation Impacts E-commerce Retailers
forces.description: New EU Regulation 2025/40 on Packaging and Packaging Waste (PPWR), effective from August 2026, introduces phased recyclability, labelling, and reporting requirements. This necessitates e-commerce retailers to assess applicable rules in each EU market, driving investment in sustainable packaging solutions and potentially increasing operational complexity.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

forces.title: Maritime Chokepoint Disruptions Cause Global Supply Chain Instability
forces.description: Disruptions at maritime chokepoints like the Strait of Hormuz lead to global supply chain instability, increased freight costs, and delays. This is a high-impact risk for retailers with international supply chains, affecting product availability, input costs, and ultimately consumer prices across various categories, highlighting the need for proactive risk management.
forces.source_title: Maritime Chokepoints: Five Lessons from the Strait of Hormuz

forces.title: AI Transforms Retail Operations and Store Network Management
forces.description: AI is increasingly embedded throughout retail operations, powering real-time decisions in frontline workflows, enhancing in-store technology, and improving order fulfillment. This technological integration enables retailers to manage their physical store networks as strategic portfolios, optimizing for role, resilience, and ecosystem value, ultimately driving productivity and competitive advantage.
forces.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

forces.title: Cost Pressures from Energy and Geopolitical Disruptions Affect Margins
forces.description: Cost pressures stemming from energy price volatility, Middle East geopolitical disruption, and US tariff uncertainty are weighing heavily on margins and investment confidence across various industries in Ireland, including the retail sector. Retailers face increased input costs and operational challenges that erode profitability.

forces.title: Automotive Retailers Face EV Transition Costs and Used-Car Value Pressure
forces.description: Irish automotive retailers must contend with the sector's reliance on government incentives and grants, the added cost burden for consumers transitioning to electric vehicles, and potential pressure on used-car values as fuel-type preferences continue to shift. These factors pose financial risks to retailers' business models and profit margins.

forces.title: Construction Recovery Boosts Household Equipment Demand
forces.description: The recovery in construction activity in Ireland is expected to provide additional support for demand across both household appliances and furniture. This linkage acts as a tailwind for retailers specializing in household equipment, as new builds and renovations drive consumer purchases of related goods.

forces.title: High Costs and Low Confidence Pressure Irish Retail Profitability
forces.description: Ireland's retail sector faces significant headwinds from rising energy costs, high rents, and labor availability challenges. These operational burdens, combined with continued pressure on real sales growth and consumer confidence, are expected to weigh on profitability and contribute to increasing insolvency levels across parts of the sector.

forces.title: Strengthening Omnichannel Capabilities Enhances Retail Resilience
forces.description: Irish retailers are encouraged to strengthen their online and omnichannel capabilities to navigate challenging trading environments. This strategic focus, coupled with careful stock management around seasonal demand peaks and tight control of operating costs, is crucial for protecting profitability and adapting to evolving consumer purchasing behaviors.

forces.title: Retail Food Prices Surge, Impacting Consumer Budgets
forces.description: Irish retail food prices have surged upwards again in 2025 and into 2026, with overall food prices 25% higher than at the start of 2022. Dairy and meat prices have increased by over one-third in the same period, significantly impacting consumer budgets and potentially dampening discretionary spending in other retail categories.
forces.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026

viewpoints.title: Dutch Retail Sales Growth Expected, but Profitability Under Increasing Pressure
viewpoints.description: ING Research forecasts a 3% increase in Dutch retail sales for 2026, with e-commerce as the primary driver at 4.5% growth. Despite improved purchasing power, consumer caution and intense price competition, coupled with rising sourcing, logistics, and labor costs, are severely impacting retailers' ability to translate sales into higher profits, leading to sustained margin pressure across the sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

viewpoints.title: Norwegian Retail Trade Supported by Tourism, but Durables Face Interest Rate Headwinds
viewpoints.description: Norges Bank's Regional Network reports solid activity in tourism and robust household finances are boosting Norway's retail trade, including consumer goods like clothing and groceries. However, the prospect of higher interest rates is dampening turnover growth in consumer durables, indicating a mixed outlook where overall retail sees support, but specific segments face challenges.
viewpoints.source_title: Regional Network report 3/2026: Minor changes in growth prospects

viewpoints.title: Irish Grocery Sales Bolstered by Weather and Events; UK Similar Performance
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland reports positive performance for grocery retailers in both Ireland and the UK. UK grocery sales grew 3.3% in the four weeks to July 12th, while Irish grocery sales saw a stronger 6.3% rise, both benefiting from warm weather and sporting events driving at-home celebrations. This indicates a favorable, albeit event-driven, short-term boost for the grocery sector.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Automotive Retail Sector Buoyant but Faces EV Transition Risks
viewpoints.description: Allianz notes Ireland's automotive retail sector shows buoyant market trends, supported by lower interest rates and competitive incentives for new and used cars. However, retailers must consider the sector's reliance on incentives, the added cost burden for consumers switching to electric vehicles, and potential pressure on used-car values as fuel-type preferences continue to shift.

viewpoints.title: AI Enables Retailers to Optimize Store Networks as Strategic Portfolios
viewpoints.description: BCG highlights that AI's integration into retail operations is revolutionizing how store networks are managed. Retailers can now treat individual locations as strategic nodes within a portfolio, moving beyond traditional store-level P&L to account for broader ecosystem value. This AI-driven approach enables enhanced measurement, capital allocation, and operational efficiency across the entire network.
viewpoints.source_title: Retailers Need to Manage Stores as a Portfolio Now. AI Lets You Do That.

viewpoints.title: Irish Community Pharmacy Sector Shows Strong Growth and Consolidation
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland reports a positive outlook for the Irish community pharmacy sector, driven by strong prescription growth, expanded clinical services, and ongoing digital investment. The sector is seeing increased M&A activity, with 98 transactions between 2023-2025, reflecting robust investor confidence and attractive long-term fundamentals as pharmacies play an increasingly vital role in primary care delivery.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish Household Equipment Sector Benefits from Construction, Faces Affordability Issues
viewpoints.description: Allianz indicates a cautiously positive outlook for Ireland's household equipment sector. It benefits from a supportive economic backdrop, recovery in construction activity, and increasing demand for energy-efficient products. However, the sector faces headwinds from softened retail sales due to higher prices and persistent cost-of-living pressures, requiring retailers and distributors to focus on value propositions and careful inventory management.

viewpoints.title: Irish Retail Sector Challenged by Declining Volumes and Cost Pressures
viewpoints.description: Allianz observes a challenging trading environment for Ireland's retail sector, marked by declining sales volumes (-0.5% YoY in April 2026) despite a modest value increase (+1.0%). While subsectors like Books, Food, Pharmaceutical Articles, and Bars perform strongly, Clothing, Department Stores, and Electrical Goods face notable declines. Rising energy costs, high rents, and labor shortages, coupled with increasing insolvencies, pressure profitability and consumer confidence.

viewpoints.title: Irish Textiles Sector Faces Headwinds but Finds Strength in Niche Segments
viewpoints.description: Allianz views Ireland's small and import-reliant textiles sector cautiously, noting its close link to overall retail demand and persistent cost pressures. While mass-market and low-cost apparel manufacturing are under pressure, stronger performance is seen in wholesale distribution and premium, sustainable, and ethical product segments. Businesses must focus on tight inventory control and cash-flow management amid rising retail insolvencies.

demand_drivers.description: Improved purchasing power is supporting overall consumer spending, although consumers remain cautious.
E-commerce remains the primary growth driver for the retail sector, consistently expanding its market share at a robust rate.

pnl_drivers.description: Consumer goods prices increased by an average of 1.5% in the first seven months of 2026, down from 2.4% a year earlier, with food inflation easing significantly. However, some categories like personal care and clothing saw modest increases, while shoes, furniture, and consumer electronics experienced price decreases.

market_sizing.methodology: ING Research forecasts Dutch retail sales to increase by 3% in 2026, with e-commerce growing 4.5%, food retail 3%, and non-food retail 2.5%. Prices for shoes, furniture, and consumer electronics were slightly lower than a year earlier, while personal care products increased 2.4% and clothing prices rose 1% in the first seven months of 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Revenue growth masks growing pressure on retail profitability in the Netherlands

demand_drivers.description: Hot weather and major sporting events boosted grocery sales, likely due to increased at-home celebrations and consumption.

pnl_drivers.description: Food inflation eased to 2.6% in the UK grocery sector, providing some relief for consumers.

market_sizing.methodology: UK Grocery sales increased by 3.3% for the four weeks to 12th July 2026. Lidl grew sales +8.6% for the 12-week period to 12th July, increasing its market share by +0.5% to 7.8%.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

demand_drivers.description: Warm weather and sporting events prompted at-home celebrations, significantly boosting Irish grocery sales.

market_sizing.methodology: Irish grocery sales grew by 6.3% for the four weeks to 12th July 2026. For the 12 weeks to 12th July, Dunnes Stores held 23.7% market share, Tesco 23.5%, SuperValu 19.6%, Lidl 14% (with 10.8% sales growth), and Aldi 11.1%.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Food and Drink Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook August 2026

demand_drivers.description: Increased demand for prescription medicines drives sales growth in community pharmacies.
The expansion of clinical services offered by pharmacies strengthens their role in primary care, increasing patient engagement and revenue.

market_sizing.methodology: Pharmaceutical sales increased by 3.9% during Q1 2026 in community pharmacies. Prescription medicine values increased by 9.5% and prescription volumes by 5% over the same period. Between 2023 and 2025, 98 pharmacy transactions were completed.
market_sizing.source_title: Bank of Ireland Healthcare Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

demand_drivers.description: Supportive financial conditions with lower interest rates encourage consumers to purchase new cars.
Retailers offer competitive incentives for both new and used cars, driving sales.
Record growth in EV registrations reflects a shift in consumer preference towards electrified vehicles.

market_sizing.methodology: Total new car registrations in Ireland reached 124,954 in 2025, a 3% increase compared to 2024. Market share by fuel type for 2025: Petrol 25.11%, Hybrid 22.48%, Electric Vehicles (EVs) 18.89%, Diesel 17.09%, Plug-In Hybrid 14.82%. New electric car registrations grew 35% over 2024.

pnl_drivers.description: Retail food prices have surged upwards in 2025 and into 2026, reaching 25% higher than early 2022 levels, significantly impacting consumer purchasing power and retail margins.

market_sizing.methodology: Irish retail food prices were 25% higher than at the outset of 2022, as of June 2026. Meat and dairy prices increased by over one-third in the same period. The FAO Monthly Food Price Index shows an upward trend in 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Mid-Year Situation and Outlook for Irish Agriculture July 2026
